<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
With `--ep` and no a2a backend, every rank gets every token, and routes to another rank's experts just have id -1. The Triton path still does work for those routes:

  - alignment keeps them in a -1 bucket, which sorts first
  - both GEMMs launch CTAs that only write zeros for them
  - quant runs over all rows
  - the combine reads all top-k slots, including the zeros

With 8 ranks, about 7 of every 8 routes are non-local on average. They contribute nothing on this rank, but at M=8192 they still take up about 27–33% of the MoE call.

 The `humming` runner already does this: it aligns with `ignore_invalid_expert=True` and combines with `moe_fused_mul_sum`, which skips negative ids (`humming.py:588`), taking the same approach on the Triton path.

Goes with the MiniMax-M2 / M2.5 `--tp 8 --ep 8` recipes on NVIDIA, which resolve to the Triton runner with `moe_a2a_backend=none`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
  - `_skip_nonlocal_routes` decides whether the skip applies: CUDA, `filter_expert`, top-k > 1, int32 contiguous `topk_ids`, and neither `no_combine` nor `defer_sum`.
  - When it's on, alignment uses `ignore_invalid_expert=True`, so
  -1 routes never reach the GEMMs.
  - FP8 quant before the down GEMM now covers routed rows only. It's the same sorted-row kernel, with `topk_ids.view(-1)` and `num_valid_tokens=E`, so -1 rows get filtered by the existing uint32 check.
  - `moe_sum_reduce_triton` takes an optional `topk_ids` and skips slots with a negative id. This is required, not just faster: `cache3` is allocated with `torch.empty`, so the skipped slots are never written.
  - The skipping path uses 4 warps instead of 16, based on a sweep on H200.

`no_combine` and `defer_sum` turn the skip off because both hand `cache3` to something else that doesn't know which slots are unwritten. Beam, the only `defer_sum` caller, already passes `filter_expert=False`, so this only guards future callers.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
No serving numbers were ran. It needs a multi-GPU EP setup, which I didn't have for this.

Still, outputs matches to the existing path: 33/33 cases across MiniMax and DSv3 shapes, including skewed routing, all-non-local routing, top-k 1 and CUDA graph replay.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Tested on a H200. Synthetic tensors at `config.json` shapes, uniform routing, rank 0 (about 12.5% of routes local), CUDA graph replay, cold L2.

  | M | MiniMax before | MiniMax after | Change | DSv3 before | DSv3 after | Change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 512 | 181.0 µs | 162.0 µs | -10.5% | 438.1 µs | 401.6 µs | -8.3% |
  | 2048 | 321.7 µs | 234.4 µs | -27.1% | 720.2 µs | 577.0 µs | -19.9% |
  | 8192 | 895.6 µs | 599.9 µs | -33.0% | 1930.5 µs | 1401.2 µs | -27.4% |
  | 16384 | 1684.3 µs | 1090.5 µs | -35.3% | 3586.0 µs | 2603.4 µs | -27.4% |

At M ≤ 64 there's no meaningful change.

Per-kernel breakdown from ncu, MiniMax M=8192, measured before rebasing onto current main:

  | Kernel | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `count_and_sort_expert_tokens_kernel` | 47.8 µs | 6.5 µs |
  | up `fused_moe_kernel` | 333.5 µs | 265.2 µs |
  | down-input quant | 70.2 µs | 23.8 µs |
  | down `fused_moe_kernel` | 243.1 µs | 174.2 µs |
  | combine | 104.3 µs | 29.2 µs |

Caveats:

- All timings use uniform routing. With skewed routing, I only checked correctness.
- Real router traces and e2e serving wasn't measured.
- found no NVIDIA DeepSeek recipe that reaches this path, so the DSv3 numbers are just kernel-level. MiniMax is actually taken from cookbook.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+
+Under expert parallelism without an all-to-all, routes to non-local experts carry
+id -1. The Triton path drops them at alignment, quantizes only routed rows, and
+the top-k combine skips their slots instead of summing zeros written for them.
+Adding +0.0 to an fp32 sum that starts at +0.0 is exact, so the whole layer is
+compared bitwise against the path that still computes those routes.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context, get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+E_GLOBAL, EP, TOPK, HIDDEN, INTER, BLOCK = 256, 8, 8, 2048, 512, [128, 128]
+E = E_GLOBAL // EP
+NUM_TOKENS = (1, 33, 300, 2048)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires CUDA")
+class TestMoeSkipNonlocalRoutes(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        cls.weights = {
+            False: (
+                (torch.randn(E, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN, device="cuda") / HIDDEN**0.5).to(
+                    torch.bfloat16
+                ),
+                (torch.randn(E, HIDDEN, INTER, device="cuda") / INTER**0.5).to(
+                    torch.bfloat16
+                ),
+                None,
+                None,
+            ),
+            True: (
+                torch.randn(E, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN, device="cuda").to(
+                    torch.float8_e4m3fn
+                ),
+                torch.randn(E, HIDDEN, INTER, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+                torch.rand(E, 2 * INTER // 128, HIDDEN // 128, device="cuda") / 32
+                + 0.01,
+                torch.rand(E, HIDDEN // 128, INTER // 128, device="cuda") / 16 + 0.02,
+            ),
+        }
+
+    def _layer(self, m, fp8, routed_scaling_factor, skip, defer_sum=False):
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.triton_utils import fused_moe
+
+        torch.manual_seed(m)
+        hidden = torch.randn(m, HIDDEN, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        global_ids = torch.rand(m, E_GLOBAL, device="cuda").topk(TOPK, dim=-1).indices
+        # This rank owns experts [0, E); every other route is -1.
+        topk_ids = torch.where(global_ids < E, global_ids, -1).to(torch.int32)
+        topk_weights = torch.rand(m, TOPK, device="cuda").softmax(-1)
+        w1, w2, w1_s, w2_s = self.weights[fp8]
+        gate = fused_moe._skip_nonlocal_routes if skip else (lambda **kw: False)
+        with mock.patch.object(fused_moe, "_skip_nonlocal_routes", gate):
+            return fused_moe.fused_experts_impl(
+                hidden,
+                w1,
+                w2,
+                topk_weights,
+                topk_ids,
+                use_fp8_w8a8=fp8,
+                w1_scale=w1_s,
+                w2_scale=w2_s,
+                block_shape=BLOCK if fp8 else None,
+                routed_scaling_factor=routed_scaling_factor,
+                filter_expert=True,
+                defer_sum=defer_sum,
+            )
+
+    def test_skipping_nonlocal_routes_is_exact(self):
+        with (
+            get_context().override_server_args(enable_deterministic_inference=False),
+            get_parallel().override(tp_group=None),
+        ):
+            for fp8 in (True, False):
+                for m in NUM_TOKENS:
+                    for rsf in (None, 2.5):
+                        with self.subTest(fp8=fp8, m=m, routed_scaling_factor=rsf):
+                            skip = self._layer(m, fp8, rsf, skip=True)
+                            ref = self._layer(m, fp8, rsf, skip=False)
+                            self.assertFalse(skip.isnan().any())
+                            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(skip, ref))
+
+    def test_defer_sum_keeps_nonlocal_routes(self):
+        # The caller sums these slots itself, so none of them may be left unwritten.
+        with (
+            get_context().override_server_args(enable_deterministic_inference=False),
+            get_parallel().override(tp_group=None),
+        ):
+            skip = self._layer(2048, False, None, skip=True, defer_sum=True)
+            ref = self._layer(2048, False, None, skip=False, defer_sum=True)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(skip, ref))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
